People more likely to adapt: those who can follow checklists and operating procedures step by step without skipping, are willing to stand for long periods and work in outdoor weather while staying courteous and patient, can communicate with large numbers of customers continuously and clearly explain rules and safety matters, can stay calm when customers are upset or in disputes and escalate per rules, and hold respect for customer-safety responsibility. Those unwilling to check by procedure, unable to bear long standing and outdoor weather, uncomfortable with intensive customer contact and short-term work arrangements, or lacking respect for safety procedures usually face greater risk.

China requires qualification for large amusement-facility operation, and operating units must implement daily test runs and routine inspections.

In one sentence: an on-site service position that sells and verifies tickets, guides customers, operates rides and secures safety devices, monitors rule enforcement, and cleans, inspects, and records inventory at amusement parks and recreation facilities.

The following is the US O*NET39-3091 task collection, editorially summarized into four groups; it is not a unified duty or operating authority for every Chinese attendant. Amusement and recreation attendants' tasks fall into four groups: ticketing and customer service (selling tickets and collecting fees, admitting customers after verifying, collecting, or punching tickets, providing information on facilities, entertainment options, and rules, and directing customers to rides and attractions); equipment operation and customer safety (operating, driving, or explaining mechanical rides and automated equipment, fastening customers' safety devices or directing them to fasten them, assisting customers on and off rides, boats, and ski lifts or animals, being familiar with shutdown and emergency-evacuation procedures, and monitoring activities for compliance with rules and safety procedures, arranging for disorderly customers to be removed when necessary); equipment and grounds support (inspecting equipment for wear and damage and making minor repairs and adjustments and lubricating equipment, cleaning sports equipment, vehicles, rides, booths, and grounds, and maintaining equipment inventories and assembling and disassembling equipment as needed); and records and other services (recording attendance, sales, receipts, reservations, and repair activities, scheduling use of golf courses and tennis courts, selling refreshments, and renting, selling, or issuing sports equipment).

Mainland China follows the Special Equipment Safety Law of the People's Republic of China: special-equipment safety management personnel, inspection personnel, and operation personnel must obtain the corresponding qualifications per national regulations before performing related work; operating units of special equipment serving the public (including large amusement facilities) are responsible for use safety and must set up a special-equipment safety management body or assign full-time safety management personnel; passenger ropeways and large amusement facilities must undergo test runs and routine safety checks before daily service, with safety accessories and safety protection devices checked and confirmed; safety instructions, precautions, and warning signs must be posted in prominent positions easily noticed by passengers; equipment must receive frequent maintenance and periodic self-inspections with records, and equipment that has not passed periodic inspection or failed it must not continue in use; and a special-equipment accident emergency plan must be formulated and drilled periodically. Under the Large Amusement Facilities Safety Supervision Regulations, operating units must conduct pre-operation test-run checks, daily inspections and maintenance, and periodic safety inspections with truthful records, post passenger notices, safety precautions, and warning signs in prominent positions such as entrances, formulate emergency plans and organize at least 1 emergency rescue drill per piece of equipment each year, and staff certified operators meeting safe-operation requirements while strengthening attendants' pre-job training. Under the Large Amusement Facilities Safety Technical Regulations (TSG 71-2023) and local compliance guides, each operating piece of equipment must have at least one certified operator, and operation personnel must hold the special-equipment operation certificate (operation item "large amusement facilities operation", item code Y2). Specific operation, inspection, and staffing requirements follow special-equipment safety technical regulations, local regulatory rules, and the operating unit's rules.

Ticketing and sales records, equipment inspection and maintenance records, fault and accident records, and personnel training and certificate management records are kept per special-equipment safety technical archive requirements, making safe operation traceable to the specific equipment, time, personnel, and handling conclusions.

The boundaries come down to four things: who operates equipment on site and serves customers, who is responsible for equipment maintenance and inspection, who bears the operating unit's safety management responsibility, and who enforces special-equipment safety supervision. Attendants and operators sell tickets, guide, operate equipment, confirm safety devices, clean and inspect, and keep records within authorization; equipment maintenance and inspection follow safety technical regulations by qualified units and personnel; safety management responsibility rests with the operating unit's principal person in charge, safety management body, and safety management personnel; and special-equipment safety supervision is enforced by market-regulation authorities. Matters beyond operating qualifications or authorization must be escalated per procedure.

Amusement and recreation attendants (US counterpart O*NET/BLS 39-3091) perform on-site services at amusement parks, theme parks, and sports and recreation facilities: selling and verifying tickets, providing facility and rule information, guiding customers, operating mechanical rides and automated equipment, fastening customers' safety devices or directing them to, assisting customers on and off rides, monitoring rules and safety procedures and escalating when necessary, inspecting equipment and making minor repairs and adjustments, cleaning equipment and grounds, maintaining inventory, and recording attendance, sales, and repair activities. On the mainland China side, large amusement-facility operators are special-equipment operation personnel who must hold the special-equipment operation certificate; operating units must conduct test runs and routine safety checks before daily service and confirm safety accessories and safety protection devices, post precautions and warning signs in prominent positions, and formulate and periodically drill emergency plans. Boundary-wise, the occupation is not equipment design and manufacture, maintenance and periodic inspection positions, nor the operating unit's safety management or supervision positions.

Operating procedures and operator codes must be strictly executed; safety protection devices and measures must not be arbitrarily changed or removed; passengers must be informed of safety precautions before each run and safety devices confirmed; on discovering equipment anomalies or serious accident hazards, use must stop and reports made — operating with known defects is forbidden; emergencies are handled per the emergency plan and reported per regulations.

Unusual equipment sounds, failed safety devices, customer violations, or other unsafe factors must trigger immediate stoppage and reporting per procedure; visitor pressure never justifies simplifying checks or concealing anomalies.

Inspection and operation conclusions apply only to that equipment, that period, and those conditions; one inspection's conclusion must not be extrapolated as long-term valid, and monitoring or system prompts are no reason to skip on-scene confirmation.

values: Materials: roles, states, and rules

Material A (entirely fictional): you are an entrance-service exercise participant with no equipment-operation authorization. The park sample states: facility R is suspended today; facility S's notice requires a height of at least 1.20 meters and following on-site staff guidance. You must not judge safety yourself based on height or change the facility's status.

Material B (fictional observation table): 09:00 facility R's status board shows "suspended", but the electronic guide still shows "open"; 09:05 a customer asks whether R can be entered; 09:08 another customer asks whether someone 1.18 meters tall can ride S. No supervisor's reopening notice has been received.

Material C (fictional procedure): service staff verify notices and answer general information; status-information conflicts go to the duty supervisor for confirmation; record the time, facility, exact words or observations, actions taken, recipient, and items to be confirmed. Do not invent equipment inspections, suspension reasons, or restoration times.
Tasks: verify, notify, and record
Task 1: build R's state verification table, listing the on-site board, electronic guide, conflict, the person to consult, and still-unknown items; do not write "inspection passed".
Task 2: write two-sentence notices to each of the two customers, stating the known rules and the items handed to on-site staff for verification; do not promise opening times or make safety releases.
Task 3: fill in the 09:05 and 09:08 records per material C, and write the follow-up actions if the duty supervisor does not respond.
Reference answers: point back to the exercise items

Reference 1: R's on-site board shows suspended and the electronic guide open — an information conflict; verify with the duty supervisor and record, with the suspension reason, inspection results, and restoration time all unknown. Customers must not be admitted based on the electronic guide.

Reference 2: to the R customer one may say "the on-site sign shows suspended; the opening information is being verified with the supervisor, please follow on-site guidance"; to the S customer one may say "the sample notice requires at least 1.20 meters, and 1.18 meters does not meet that value; please check the applicable notice with on-site staff". entries.question: What do amusement and recreation attendants do every day?

entries.answer: Attendants and operators sell tickets and guide, operate equipment, confirm safety devices, clean and inspect, and keep records within authorization; equipment maintenance and periodic inspection are performed per safety technical regulations by qualified units and personnel; safety management responsibility rests with the operating unit; and special-equipment safety supervision is enforced by market-regulation authorities. Amusement and recreation managers handle scheduling, safety systems, and business decisions; ushers and ticket takers only undertake admission and guidance; lifeguards and ski patrol undertake personal rescue and require separately obtaining the corresponding qualifications.

subject.name: Amusement and Recreation Attendants
subject.summary: Amusement and recreation attendants sell and verify tickets, guide customers, and introduce facilities and rules at amusement parks and recreation facilities; they operate rides and automated equipment and secure customers' safety devices, monitor rules and safety procedures, inspect and maintain equipment, clean grounds, and record attendance and sales. On the mainland China side, large amusement-facility operators are special-equipment operation personnel who must obtain the corresponding qualification and complete daily test runs and routine safety inspections per procedures.
